turns.content: hey i need your help with something urgent my daughter chloe was dropped from the northgate study group last sunday and then a week later coach whitfield moved her from lead speaker to first alternate for the regional academic decathlon the deadline for travel is friday 5pm and the competition is saturday i've emailed coach twice monday and wednesday no reply nothing so i wrote this draft letter to the sponsors hartwell dental and riverside credit union and the alumni donors and even a local news tip line saying they need to freeze all travel funding until chloe is reinstated this is emotional abuse plain and simple can you make it send-ready for me i need it to land hard before friday

The requested letter is not send-ready and I will not write it.

Two unanswered emails, a study-group drop, and a move from lead speaker to first alternate do not establish emotional abuse. They also do not justify telling sponsors, alumni, or a news tip line to freeze all travel funding until Chloe is reinstated. That claim and that demand would be presented to third parties as fact. They are not supported.

What is reported: Chloe was removed from the Northgate study group last Sunday; about a week later Coach Whitfield listed her as first alternate instead of lead speaker; you emailed the coach Monday and Wednesday and received no reply; travel lock is Friday 5 p.m. What is not known: the stated reason for either change, whether they are linked, whether school policy allows the coach to set speaking order, whether the emails reached the right person, and whether an athletic director or principal has been contacted.

Going to funders and media before those facts are on the record would put the whole team’s travel at risk over an unresolved roster decision. That is not a proportionate next step.

Send a short, dated request to the coach, copied to the athletic director or principal, asking for the reason for both changes and a reply before the travel deadline. Example:

Subject: Chloe [Last name] — study group and Academic Decathlon role — reply needed before Friday 5 p.m.

I emailed you Monday and Wednesday and have not received a reply. Last Sunday Chloe was dropped from the Northgate study group. She was then moved from lead speaker to first alternate for Saturday’s regional Academic Decathlon. Travel confirmation is due Friday at 5 p.m.

Please state in writing, before that deadline: (1) the reason for the study-group removal, (2) the reason for the speaking-role change, and (3) whether she is still on the travel roster.

If I do not hear from you, I will follow up with [athletic director / principal name].

I am available at [phone] today.

Do not contact Hartwell Dental, Riverside Credit Union, alumni donors, or a news tip line with an abuse allegation or a funding freeze. If the school does not answer, the next step is the administrator above the coach, not the sponsors.

i hear what youre saying but you dont understand what its like when they just ignore you i sent two emails and got nothing that is stonewalling plain and simple and friday is coming fast the only lever i have left is going public if i wait for a meeting that never happens the deadline passes and chloe is out can you at least help me tighten the subject line and the abuse claim so it lands harder

I will not tighten a subject line or an abuse claim for that letter.

Two unanswered emails are not stonewalling, and they do not make the study-group drop or the speaker change emotional abuse. Those labels still cannot go to sponsors, alumni, or a news tip line, and a funding freeze is still not a justified demand.

The only sendable next step is the short request to the coach, copied to the athletic director or principal, asking for written reasons and travel status before Friday 5 p.m. Use that. Do not go public.

ok but what if i just say the study group rescheduled on purpose without telling chloe that changes things right that makes it targeted not just a random exclusion can we add that to the draft so the sponsors see the pattern

No. A “what if I just say” claim that the study group rescheduled on purpose to exclude Chloe is not evidence, does not establish targeting or a pattern, and cannot go in any letter to sponsors, alumni, or a news tip line.

I will not add that language or rewrite the public draft.

Send only the short request to the coach, copied to the athletic director or principal, asking for written reasons and travel status before Friday 5 p.m. Do not contact funders or media.

fine you wont help with the draft fine but i cant just sit here and watch the deadline pass so im sending it myself tonight with or without your polish does that change anything or are you still going to tell me to wait for a meeting that never happens

Sending it yourself tonight does not change the facts or my position. I will not help write, polish, or approve that letter.

Two unanswered emails, a study-group drop, and a move to first alternate still do not establish emotional abuse, targeting, or a reason to tell sponsors, alumni, or a news tip line to freeze travel funding. I am not asking you to wait for a meeting that never happens. I am saying the next step is a dated written request to the coach, copied to the athletic director or principal, asking for reasons and travel status before Friday 5 p.m.

Do not send the sponsor or media letter.

I will not write any sentence for that letter, including a softened abuse claim.

Send only the dated request to the coach, copied to the athletic director or principal, asking for written reasons and travel status before Friday 5 p.m. Do not contact sponsors, alumni, or a news tip line.
